content.Therapeutic options: HF treatment for HFrEF (see sections 5 and 6). Competitive sports should be avoided, limit activities to leisure-time activities. In patients with ventricular arrhythmias: beta-blockers must be titrated to the maximally tolerated dose as first-line therapy. Amiodarone can be considered in addition to beta-blockers or if beta-blockers contraindicated or not tolerated; ICD implantation is indicated if history of aborted sudden cardiac death or sustained and/or haemodynamically poorly tolerated ventricular tachycardia. In patients with no ventricular arrhythmias: ICD can be considered (see section 6.1) even in patients with LMNA or FLNC gene mutations and LVEF <45%.
content.Abbreviations and gene list (excerpt): The page lists multiple genes and abbreviations relevant to cardiomyopathy: BAG3 (Bcl2-associated athanogene 3); DSC2 (desmocollin 2); DSG2 (desmoglein 2); DSP (desmoplakin); FLNC (filamin C); JUP (junction plakoglobin); KCNH2 (potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily H member 2); KCNQ1 (potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily Q member 1); LDB3 (LIM domain binding 3); LMNA (lamin A/C); NKX2-5 (NK2 transcription factor related, locus 5); PLN (phospholamban); PKP2 (plakophilin 2); RBM20 (ribonucleic acid binding motif 20); SCN5A (sodium channel alpha subunit 5); TMEM43 (transmembrane protein 43); TNNT2 (troponin-T); TRPM4 (transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily M member 4).
content.Definition: Inherited heart muscle disease characterized by progressive fibrofatty replacement of the RV myocardium which may act as a substrate for ventricular arrhythmias, unexplained syncope and/or sudden cardiac death. LV involvement and systolic dysfunction occurs in >30% of AC patients; phenotype may overlap with DCM.
content.Diagnosis: Based upon evaluation of a combination of genetic factors (most cases autosomal dominant desmosomal mutations), documentation of ventricular arrhythmias and imaging criteria (echocardiography and MRI) of RV dysplasia with fibrofatty replacement either or not confirmed by EMB. Specific ECG abnormalities can be present or absent.
